{{Quote|Are you the Jedi responsible for this intrusion, Shorttail?''"<br />"''Who askz?''"<br />"''Colonel Retk. Colonel ''Wruq'' Retk. Commander of this facility.|Wruq Retk and Saba Sebatyne|<ref name="Abyss" />}}
'''Wruq Retk''' was a [[Yaka]] [[Colonel/Legends|colonel]] in [[Galactic Alliance Security]]. He [[Commander/Legends|commanded]] a [[Galactic Alliance Security Detention Center 81|secret]] [[Galactic Alliance Security blockhouse]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where [[Force psychosis|psychotic]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Valin Horn]] and [[Jysella Horn]] were [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|frozen]] in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]. In [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]], the [[Jedi High Council (New Jedi Order)|Jedi Council]] acquired a document granting the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] access to the blockhouse to see the two Knights. A contingent of Jedi, accompanied by the [[Horn family|Horns']] [[Parent/Legends|mother]], [[Mirax Terrik Horn]], and several [[Journalist/Legends|journalists]], entered the facility, where they found the two carbonite-imprisoned Jedi on display above a large [[Aquarium/Legends|aquarium]]. Retk arrived shortly after and attempted to take control of the situation, but Terrik Horn, furious at him for mistreating her [[Youngling/Legends|children]], assaulted him and knocked the larger Yaka out with one blow.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Tell me, Captain Xanda, does GAS really intend to charge a bereaved mother with assault? A distraught, ''fifty-kilogram'' mother who resorted to ''slapping'' a Yaka colonel ''three'' times her size&mdash;''after'' she discovered he has been hanging her children on the wall&hellip;as ''office decorations''?|Javis Tyrr, to Captain Xanda, on Wruq Retk|<ref name="Abyss" />}}
Wruq Retk was a [[Yaka]] who served as a [[Colonel/Legends|colonel]] in [[Galactic Alliance Security]].<ref name="Abyss" /> In [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=222689&start=7260#17384444|thread=Books, Comics, & Television VIPs|user=[[Sue Rostoni]]|date=2008-10-02|time=10:48 AM}} dates the beginning of the [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series to [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]]. As ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]'', the third installment of the series, is dated to 43 ABY by ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', its events must take place in 43.5 ABY.</ref> he was the [[Commander/Legends|commander]] of<ref name="Abyss" /> [[Galactic Alliance Security Detention Center 81|Detention Center 81]],<ref name="Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref> a secret [[Galactic Alliance Security blockhouse]] on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Valin Horn]] and [[Jysella Horn]], who had come down with an [[Force psychosis|enigmatic madness]], were captured by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], and, after being [[The Galactic Federation of Free Alliances versus Valin Horn|deemed]] too dangerous to be confined in a conventional [[Prison/Legends|prison]], they were [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|encased]] in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and eventually placed in the blockhouse that Retk commanded. Retk decided to keep them on display over a large [[Aquarium/Legends|aquarium]] in the lobby outside the facility's executive offices. Shortly after the formation of the [[Court of Jedi Affairs]] by Galactic Alliance [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Natasi Daala]], the Court's head, [[Arabelle Lorteli]], signed a document giving [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] permission to enter Retk's blockhouse and see the captive Knights.<ref name="Abyss" />

[[File:Saba_Sebatyne_by_Brian_Rood.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Wruq Retk came into conflict with Jedi Master Saba Sebatyne (picutred) while holding two psychotic Jedi Knights captive.]]
A group of Jedi, including [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Saba Sebatyne]], Jedi Knight [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], and the [[Horn family|Horns']] [[Parent/Legends|father]], [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]], were accompanied by the Horns' mother, [[Mirax Terrik Horn]], and a large contingent of [[Journalist/Legends|journalists]], including [[Javis Tyrr]]. Galactic Alliance Security forces attempted to prevent the Jedi access to the blockhouse, but to no avail. Retk quickly arrived on the scene, however, insulting Sebatyne with the hopes of provoking the Jedi Master to attack him in front of the press. However, Retk was instantly confronted by Terrik Horn, who accused him of using her [[Youngling/Legends|children]] as "decorations"&mdash;which he denied, claiming he only wished to keep them where he could personally oversee their maintenance&mdash;and abruptly hit him, knocking Retk unconscious in one blow. A Security [[Captain/Legends|captain]], [[Xanda]], began to call for the arrest of Terrik Horn for assaulting Retk, but Daala arrived and took control of the situation, declaring that Terrik Horn would not be punished.<ref name="Abyss" /> 

In [[44 ABY]],<ref name="Date 2">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]'' and ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]'' to [[44 ABY]].</ref> Daala recalled the incident with the Jedi and Retk during a morning briefing surrounding the [[Trial of Tahiri Veila|trial]] of Jedi Knight [[Tahiri Veila]] after [[Judge/Legends|Judge]] Lorteli was mentioned.<ref name="Allies">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref> Later that [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="Date 2" /> when members of the [[Solo family/Legends|Solo family]], alongside the Jedi Knight [[Zekk]] and his [[Marriage/Legends|fiancée]] [[Taryn Zel]], went on a [[Raid on Detention Center 81|mission]] to free Valin and Jesella Horn from the Galactic Alliance's captivity, Zel suspected that the organization had increased their security precautions after Jaina and the other Jedi had embarrassed Retk. When they later discovered that the Alliance had been capturing many Jedi, Jaina suggested that it was possible Retk was kidnapping the Jedi, not Daala.<ref name="Vortex" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|If you're the commander of this toxiden, then you must be the son-of-a-schutta who decided to use my children as decorations.''"<br />"''Please, it's not meant to insult them. I just wanted to put them where I could see to their maintenance ''personally''.''"<br />"''The ''kriff'' you did.|Mirax Terrik Horn and Wruq Retk|<ref name="Abyss" />}}
Like most Yaka, Wruq Retk had large arms and a [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] [[Brain/Legends|brain]] [[Cyborg/Legends|implant]] that enhanced his intelligence. He was rude and abrasive [[Anti-Jedi sentiment/Legends|toward]] the Jedi and intentionally attempted to provoke Jedi Master Saba Sebatyne into attacking him, an act that would have, under normal circumstances, resulted in his arm being [[Dismemberment/Legends|severed]] by the Barabel Jedi Master and then used to beat him around the head. He was also callous toward the Horn family; he hung their two carbonite-imprisoned children on his wall as office decorations and was amused by Terrik Horn's distress. However, he underestimated the grief and anger of Mirax Terrik Horn, who punched him out cold.<ref name="Abyss" />

==Equipment==
Retk wore a Galactic Alliance Security [[Clothing/Legends|uniform]] that indicated he was a colonel.<ref name="Abyss" />

==Behind the scenes==
Wruq Retk first appeared in [[Troy Denning]]'s [[2009]] novel ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]'', the third installment in the [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series.<ref name="Abyss" />
